title: NXT Outlook Console
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: NXT Outlook Console
Thesis: An executive intelligence dashboard pairing every 2026 insurance recommendation with the market and social-listening evidence that justifies it.
Why this frame: Insurance strategy leaders expect a synthesized outlook deliverable with drill-down evidence, honoring how strategy decks and research portals conventionally work. It removes the trust gap between AI recommendations and board accountability.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Dana Reyes
  Role: VP of Strategy, mid-size P&C carrier (~$2.4B GWP)
  Context: Building the 2026 strategic planning narrative for a board with low risk tolerance and high skepticism of black-box AI. She has three weeks before the offsite and a research budget already spent on six fragmented vendor reports.
  Emotional state: Time-pressured and defensive — she must defend every claim in a room of actuarial skeptics, and a single unsupported assertion can derail her credibility.
  Pain points:
    - AI tools produce confident recommendations with no traceable provenance, making them unciteable in board materials
    - Synthesizing six vendor reports plus social-listening feeds into a coherent outlook takes her analysts two full weeks
    - Sentiment and market-signal data live in separate tools that never reconcile against one another
    - She cannot quickly compare which recommendations are well-supported versus speculative when prioritizing the deck
  JTBD: When I assemble the 2026 outlook for my board, I want every strategic recommendation backed by inspectable, citable evidence, so I can defend each one under scrutiny and ship a deck I trust.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Strategy Analyst (Marcus): Drills into evidence stacks, flags weak recommendations for deeper review, validates citations before export
  - Chief Underwriting Officer: Consumes the confidence-scored themes to stress-test underwriting-relevant shifts
  - Board Member / Audit Committee: Reviews exported sections, occasionally clicks through to provenance to verify a claim
  - Market Research Vendor: Source of ingested syndicated reports surfaced in provenance views
  - Compliance Reviewer: Audits citation accuracy and ensures social-listening data usage is policy-compliant

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Dana reviews the top five recommended 2026 strategic shifts, expands the 'Embedded climate-parametric products' recommendation to inspect its supporting research excerpts and a two-year sentiment trendline, sees a 0.84 confidence score with full source coverage, then exports a board-ready section with auto-generated citations attached.

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Read the 2026 outlook executive summary
     Trigger: Dana opens the console Monday morning to begin drafting the board narrative
     Flow: Lands on Outlook Overview → scans five ranked strategic recommendations with one-line theses → reads the synthesized market-context paragraph → notes the confidence badge color on each card → clicks into the highest-priority one
     AI role: Synthesis engine clusters thousands of source signals into five ranked recommendation themes and drafts the executive narrative in Dana's house voice
     Outcome: Dana has a defensible top-five framing in under five minutes instead of two weeks of analyst synthesis
  2. Expand a recommendation to its evidence stack
     Trigger: Dana wants to know why the console recommends embedded climate-parametric products
     Flow: Clicks a recommendation card → Evidence Panel slides in from the right → sees grouped evidence (market reports, sentiment shifts, competitor moves) → expands each cluster → reads pull-quotes with relevance scores
     AI role: Evidence-to-recommendation linking maps each supporting signal to the claim it justifies, ranked by relevance and recency
     Outcome: Dana sees the full proof chain behind a recommendation without leaving the screen
  3. Trace a claim to its market-research source
     Trigger: A board member will likely ask 'says who?' about a specific assertion
     Flow: Within Evidence Panel clicks a pull-quote → Source Provenance View opens → sees publisher, publication date, methodology note, and the exact passage highlighted in context → copies a citation
     AI role: Citation generation formats a complete, board-grade reference from source metadata; RAG retrieval surfaces the exact passage
     Outcome: Dana can answer 'says who?' instantly with publisher, date, and verbatim source
  4. Inspect social-listening sentiment shifts
     Trigger: A recommendation hinges on shifting consumer attitudes toward usage-based coverage
     Flow: Opens Sentiment Trend Explorer → selects the theme → sees a 24-month sentiment trendline with annotated inflection points → toggles consumer vs broker vs press segments → reads what drove each inflection
     AI role: Sentiment shift detection identifies statistically significant inflections and labels probable drivers from concurrent events
     Outcome: Dana grounds an attitudinal claim in a quantified, time-anchored sentiment movement
  5. Compare recommendation confidence across themes
     Trigger: Dana must decide which three of five recommendations lead the deck
     Flow: Opens Theme Comparison Grid → sees all recommendations on a confidence × impact matrix → sorts by evidence coverage → identifies which are well-supported vs speculative → reorders her priority list
     AI role: Confidence scoring computes a composite from source quantity, quality, recency, and signal agreement per theme
     Outcome: Dana prioritizes the deck by defensibility, not just intuition
  6. Flag a recommendation for deeper analyst review
     Trigger: One recommendation looks promising but thinly supported
     Flow: Clicks 'Flag for review' on the card → adds a note about the concern → assigns to Marcus → flag appears in his queue with the evidence gap highlighted
     AI role: AI annotates the flag with the specific evidence gaps (e.g., 'single source, no sentiment corroboration') it detects
     Outcome: Weak recommendations get human validation before they reach the board
  7. Assemble a board-ready outlook section
     Trigger: Dana is ready to convert console insights into deck-ready content
     Flow: Opens Export Builder → drags selected recommendations into a section outline → reorders → AI drafts narrative prose per section → Dana edits inline → previews the formatted section
     AI role: Synthesis engine drafts board-appropriate prose with embedded citations and pulls a representative sentiment chart per section
     Outcome: Dana produces a polished, citation-backed board section in minutes
  8. Export and cite the synthesized findings
     Trigger: The section is finalized and needs to leave the console
     Flow: Clicks Export → selects format (PowerPoint, PDF, Notion) → reviews auto-attached citation appendix → confirms → receives the file with a provenance footnote per claim
     AI role: Citation generation compiles a complete, deduplicated reference appendix and links each in-text claim to its source
     Outcome: Dana exports a fully attributed deliverable that survives audit and board scrutiny
  9. Detect a contradicting signal across sources
     Trigger: Two ingested reports disagree on a market trajectory
     Flow: Recommendation card shows a 'contested' badge → Dana expands → Evidence Panel shows both sides with the disagreement explained → she decides how to frame the nuance
     AI role: Synthesis engine flags conflicting signals and surfaces the dissent rather than averaging it away
     Outcome: Dana avoids overstating consensus and frames contested themes honestly
  10. Set a watch on an emerging theme
     Trigger: A sub-threshold theme is gaining sentiment momentum but not yet a top-five recommendation
     Flow: Opens a 'rising signals' tray → spots an emerging theme → clicks 'Watch' → defines a confidence threshold → console alerts when it crosses
     AI role: Continuous monitoring re-scores emerging themes against the watch threshold as new data ingests
     Outcome: Dana catches the next strategic shift before competitors do
  11. Annotate a recommendation with internal context
     Trigger: Dana knows an internal capacity constraint the model cannot see
     Flow: Adds a private annotation to a recommendation card → tags relevant colleagues → annotation persists alongside AI evidence → appears in export as an internal note (excludable)
     AI role: AI distinguishes internal annotations from sourced evidence and keeps them clearly separated in exports
     Outcome: Human institutional knowledge enriches AI output without contaminating provenance
  12. Refresh the outlook against new data
     Trigger: A major industry report drops two days before the offsite
     Flow: Clicks 'Refresh' → console re-ingests and re-scores → diff view shows which recommendations moved and why → Dana reviews the deltas → re-exports only changed sections
     AI role: Incremental synthesis recomputes scores and surfaces a changelog of what shifted and the driving new evidence
     Outcome: Dana's outlook stays current to the last minute without a full rebuild

KEY SCREENS (10) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Outlook Overview - purpose: Present the ranked top-five 2026 recommendations with confidence badges and the synthesized market narrative as the landing canvas
     Primary element: Five vertically-stacked recommendation cards with confidence color-coding and one-line theses, anchored by a synthesized summary band
     Motion character: Cards settle in with a staggered 60ms cascade; confidence badges fade their fill on first paint to signal computation
  2. Recommendation Detail with Evidence Panel - purpose: Reveal the full evidence stack justifying a single recommendation
     Primary element: A right-sliding panel with grouped evidence clusters (market reports, sentiment, competitor signals), each expandable to pull-quotes
     Motion character: Panel slides in over 320ms with the recommendation card staying pinned-left; clusters accordion open with spring physics
  3. Source Provenance View - purpose: Show the exact source passage, publisher metadata, and methodology behind a single claim
     Primary element: A document-context viewer with the cited passage highlighted in situ and a metadata sidebar
     Motion character: Highlighted passage pulses once on load to orient the eye; metadata sidebar reveals top-down
  4. Sentiment Trend Explorer - purpose: Visualize 24-month sentiment trendlines with annotated inflection points across audience segments
     Primary element: An interactive multi-series line chart with annotation callouts and segment toggles
     Motion character: Lines draw left-to-right over 800ms; annotation pins drop with a slight bounce at inflections
  5. Theme Comparison Grid - purpose: Let Dana compare all recommendations on a confidence × impact matrix to prioritize the deck
     Primary element: A scatter matrix with recommendation bubbles sized by evidence coverage, with sort and filter controls
     Motion character: Bubbles animate to their coordinates on sort change with 400ms eased transitions
  6. Confidence & Coverage Indicator - purpose: Explain how a confidence score was computed so the number is itself defensible
     Primary element: A breakdown card showing source count, quality weighting, recency, and signal-agreement contributions to the composite score
     Motion character: Contribution bars fill sequentially to narrate the composite; total counts up numerically
  7. Export Builder - purpose: Assemble selected recommendations into a board-ready section with AI-drafted prose and citations
     Primary element: A two-pane builder: draggable section outline on the left, live formatted preview on the right
     Motion character: Drag interactions snap with tactile easing; AI-drafted prose types in with a subtle shimmer to signal generation
  8. Rising Signals Tray - purpose: Surface sub-threshold emerging themes Dana can place on watch
     Primary element: A collapsible bottom tray of momentum chips with mini sparklines and watch toggles
     Motion character: Tray slides up from bottom; sparklines animate momentum direction on hover
  9. Refresh Diff View - purpose: Show what changed after re-ingesting new data and why
     Primary element: A changelog with before/after confidence deltas and the new evidence that moved each recommendation
     Motion character: Changed values cross-fade old→new with a directional arrow; unchanged items dim back
  10. Analyst Flag Queue - purpose: Let Marcus triage flagged recommendations with their AI-detected evidence gaps
     Primary element: A queue list with each flag's note, assignee, and the highlighted evidence gap
     Motion character: Resolved items slide out left; new flags slide in with a soft attention pulse

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Cross-source synthesis engine
     User action: Opens the console or clicks Refresh
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Ingested market-research reports, social-listening feeds, competitor disclosures, internal annotations
     Output: Five ranked strategic recommendation themes with synthesized narrative prose in Dana's house voice
     User benefit: Replaces two weeks of analyst synthesis with a defensible top-five framing in minutes
  2. Evidence-to-recommendation linking (headline aha)
     User action: Clicks any recommendation card
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: The recommendation claim plus the full ingested source corpus with embeddings
     Output: Ranked, grouped evidence clusters with pull-quotes and per-quote relevance scores mapped to the claim
     User benefit: Every recommendation is one click from the proof behind it — the trust unlock
  3. Sentiment shift detection
     User action: Opens the Sentiment Trend Explorer or views a card with attitudinal claims
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: 24 months of segmented social-listening and press sentiment time-series
     Output: Statistically significant inflection points with labeled probable drivers per audience segment
     User benefit: Grounds soft attitudinal claims in quantified, time-anchored movement Dana can defend
  4. Confidence & coverage scoring
     User action: Views any recommendation card or the Comparison Grid
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Per-recommendation source count, source quality weights, recency, and cross-signal agreement
     Output: A composite 0–1 confidence score with an explainable contribution breakdown
     User benefit: Lets Dana prioritize the deck by defensibility and explain the score itself if challenged
  5. Citation generation
     User action: Clicks a source or exports a section
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Source metadata (publisher, date, methodology, passage location)
     Output: Board-grade formatted citations and a deduplicated reference appendix linked to each in-text claim
     User benefit: Produces audit-surviving attribution automatically, eliminating manual citation labor
  6. Conflict & contested-signal detection
     User action: Reviews recommendations on the Overview
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Cross-source signals scored for directional agreement
     Output: A 'contested' badge and a both-sides explanation where sources materially disagree
     User benefit: Prevents Dana from overstating consensus and lets her frame nuance honestly
  7. Board-ready prose drafting
     User action: Drags recommendations into the Export Builder outline
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Selected recommendations, their evidence, and Dana's tone preferences
     Output: Polished board-section narrative with embedded inline citations and a representative chart per section
     User benefit: Turns console insight into a finished, citation-backed deliverable in minutes
  8. Emerging-theme watch monitoring
     User action: Sets a watch threshold on a rising signal
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Sub-threshold theme signals re-scored against newly ingested data
     Output: Threshold-crossing alerts with the evidence that drove the momentum
     User benefit: Lets Dana catch the next strategic shift before it becomes obvious to competitors

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: data-dense editorial restraint, enterprise-blue authority, evidentiary calm, board-grade typographic hierarchy, provenance-first information architecture
  Hero treatment: The Outlook Overview leads with a quiet, confident masthead — a deep ink-blue header band with the carrier-neutral wordmark, beneath which five recommendation cards sit on a generous off-white canvas. Each card pairs an action-oriented title with a single restrained confidence badge (a thin ring, not a loud chip), signaling that rigor, not flash, is the product's value. Whitespace is deliberate and editorial, evoking a research journal rather than a dashboard.
  Motion character: Motion is purposeful and never decorative — every animation narrates a computation (bars fill to show scoring, lines draw to show trend, ghost cards travel to show assembly). Easing is calm and slightly heavy, conveying that the system is deliberate. Nothing bounces gratuitously; the single amber passage-pulse is the only attention-grabbing gesture, reserved for provenance.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. An abstract editorial illustration of interlinked evidence nodes converging into a single recommendation, deep ink-blue on cream, flat vector style
    2. A muted hero background of layered translucent data strata suggesting synthesis depth, no text, enterprise-blue palette
    3. A subtle empty-state illustration of a magnifying glass over a document passage, line-art, low-saturation
    4. A decorative section divider depicting a sentiment trendline rising through annotated inflection markers, minimal and editorial
    5. An onboarding spot illustration of a confident strategist presenting a cited chart to a boardroom, flat geometric, restrained palette
    6. A success-state graphic of a sealed, footnoted document with provenance ribbons, clean vector, blue and gold accents

  2. Phase 2 (Month 2) - Intelligence & Defensibility

  1. Minute 1
     User: Dana opens the console and sees five ranked 2026 recommendations with confidence badges and a synthesized summary
     AI: Synthesis engine has already clustered thousands of signals into ranked themes and drafted the narrative
     Feeling: Relief — the blank-page dread of starting the deck dissolves into a credible starting frame
  2. Minute 5
     User: She clicks the climate-parametric recommendation and the Evidence Panel reveals eleven supporting signals with pull-quotes
     AI: Evidence-to-recommendation linking maps each signal to the claim with a relevance score
     Feeling: Trust ignites — for the first time an AI recommendation shows its work
  3. Day 1
     User: Dana traces a claim to its exact source passage and copies a board-grade citation
     AI: RAG retrieval surfaces the verbatim passage; citation generation formats the reference
     Feeling: Confidence — she can now answer 'says who?' instantly
  4. Day 3
     User: She uses the Comparison Grid to demote a thinly-supported recommendation and flags it for Marcus
     AI: Confidence scoring and gap detection expose which themes are speculative
     Feeling: Control — she prioritizes by defensibility, not gut
  5. Week 1
     User: Dana assembles three sections in the Export Builder and ships a citation-backed board deck
     AI: Prose drafting and citation appendix compile the deliverable
     Feeling: Pride — the deck looks like it took two weeks; it took an afternoon
  6. Month 1
     User: A late industry report drops; Dana hits Refresh and reviews only what changed via the Diff View
     AI: Incremental synthesis re-scores and surfaces a precise changelog
     Feeling: Calm — staying current no longer means starting over
  7. Month 3+
     User: A watched emerging theme crosses its threshold and alerts Dana before competitors react
     AI: Watch monitoring re-scores sub-threshold signals continuously
     Feeling: Foresight — the console has become her early-warning radar

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (12 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Dana hovers the 'Launch embedded climate-parametric products' card on the Outlook Overview
     System: Card lifts subtly and its confidence badge reveals the numeric score on hover
     Motion/feedback: 2px lift with soft shadow bloom; badge fill animates (150ms)
  2. She clicks the card
     System: Card pins to the left; the Evidence Panel begins sliding in from the right edge
     Motion/feedback: Panel slide-in with eased deceleration; page content dims 10% (320ms)
  3. Dana waits as the panel settles
     System: Three evidence clusters render — Market Reports (5), Sentiment (3), Competitor Signals (3) — with a coverage badge reading 'Full'
     Motion/feedback: Cluster headers cascade in at 60ms intervals; coverage badge counts up (400ms)
  4. She expands the Market Reports cluster
     System: Five pull-quotes accordion open, each with a relevance score bar and recency tag
     Motion/feedback: Spring-physics accordion; relevance bars fill left-to-right (280ms)
  5. Dana clicks the top pull-quote ('Parametric premium volume projected to grow double digits')
     System: Source Provenance View opens overlaying the panel, showing the passage highlighted in document context
     Motion/feedback: Overlay fades up; highlighted passage pulses once amber (300ms)
  6. She reads the publisher, date, and methodology note in the sidebar
     System: Metadata sidebar populates with quality-weight indicator at 0.93
     Motion/feedback: Sidebar reveals top-down; quality dial sweeps to position (350ms)
  7. Dana clicks 'Copy citation'
     System: A board-grade formatted citation copies to clipboard and a confirmation toast appears
     Motion/feedback: Toast slides up from bottom with checkmark; button briefly state-changes to 'Copied' (200ms)
  8. She closes provenance and clicks the Confidence indicator on the panel header
     System: Confidence & Coverage breakdown expands showing source-count, quality, recency, and agreement contributions summing to 0.84
     Motion/feedback: Contribution bars fill sequentially; total number counts up to 0.84 (600ms)
  9. Dana clicks 'Add to export'
     System: The recommendation drops into the Export Builder outline with its evidence and citations attached
     Motion/feedback: A ghost card animates from the panel toward the export tab badge, which increments (400ms)
  10. She opens the Export Builder
     System: AI-drafted board prose types into the section preview with embedded citation markers
     Motion/feedback: Prose types with a subtle shimmer; citation superscripts fade in as anchors resolve (900ms)
  11. Dana clicks Export → PowerPoint
     System: The file generates with a provenance footnote per claim and a reference appendix
     Motion/feedback: Progress ring completes; download chip slides in with file name (700ms)
  12. She reviews the citation appendix in the preview
     System: Deduplicated references list renders, each linking back to its source passage
     Motion/feedback: Appendix items fade in; hover on any reference highlights its in-text anchor (300ms)

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - Dana can trace any top-five recommendation to a cited source passage in two clicks or fewer
  - Every recommendation card displays an explainable confidence score with a contribution breakdown
  - Contested signals are visibly badged rather than averaged into false consensus
  - A complete, citation-backed board section can be assembled and exported in under 15 minutes
  - 100% of exported claims carry a provenance footnote linking to source metadata
  - Refreshing against new data surfaces a precise changelog of which recommendations moved and why
  - An emerging watched theme triggers an alert before it would surface organically in a top-five list

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
  Brand: (unset)
  Platform: web
  Accessibility: WCAG AA
  Other:
    - No verbatim source quotes longer than 80 characters in any rendered field
    - Internal annotations must be visually and structurally separable from sourced evidence in all exports
    - All AI providers must have a multi-provider fallback path
    - Citation formatting must survive export to PPTX, PDF, and Notion without loss of provenance links

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are the cross-source synthesis engine for a P&C insurance strategy console. Cluster ingested market reports, social-listening feeds, competitor disclosures, and internal annotations into five ranked 2026 strategic recommendation themes. Draft a concise executive narrative in a measured, board-grade house voice. Never invent sources; ground every theme in supplied signals.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Synthesize the 2026 outlook for a mid-size P&C carrier (~$2.4B GWP). Source corpus: {sources}. Evidence signals: {evidence_items}. Internal annotations: {annotations}. Return five ranked recommendations with one-line theses and a synthesized market-context paragraph.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { summary_narrative: string, recommendations: [{ id, title, thesis, theme, rank, drafted_narrative }] }

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a RAG evidence-linking engine. Given a recommendation claim and the ingested source corpus with embeddings, retrieve and group supporting/contradicting signals into clusters (Market Reports, Sentiment, Competitor Signals, Internal Annotations). Score each by relevance and recency. Paraphrase pull-quotes to ≤80 characters — never verbatim.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Recommendation: {recommendation_title} — {thesis}. Corpus: {evidence_items_for_recommendation}. Return grouped, ranked evidence clusters with paraphrased pull-quotes (≤80 chars), relevance_score, recency_days, and signal_direction.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { clusters: [{ name, count, items: [{ pull_quote, source_id, relevance_score, recency_days, signal_direction }] }], coverage_status }

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Open explorer or click attitudinal evidence item
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a sentiment shift-detection engine. Given 24-month segmented sentiment time-series, identify statistically significant inflection points and label probable drivers from concurrent industry events. Operate per audience segment (consumer, broker, press).
ai_flows.user_message_template: Theme: {theme}. Segment series: {monthly_values_by_segment}. Identify inflection points (month index + probable driver label) and compute net_change and current_score per segment.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { series: [{ segment, monthly_values[24], inflection_points: [{ month, label }], net_change, current_score }] }

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Card render / Confidence indicator click / Comparison Grid load / Refresh
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a confidence-scoring engine. Compute a composite 0–1 confidence per recommendation from source count, source quality weights, recency, and cross-signal agreement. Return an explainable contribution breakdown so the score itself is defensible.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Recommendation: {recommendation_id}. Inputs — source_count: {n}, quality_weights: {weights}, recency_days: {recency}, signal_agreement: {agreement}. Return composite confidence_score and per-factor contributions.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { confidence_score: number, coverage_status: string, contributions: [{ factor, weight, value }] }

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Open provenance view / Copy citation / Export
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a citation-generation engine producing board-grade references. From source metadata (publisher, date, methodology, passage location), format a complete citation and compile a deduplicated reference appendix. Each in-text claim links to its source. Citation format must survive PPTX, PDF, and Notion export without losing provenance links.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Source metadata: {source}. Claim: {claim}. Format a board-grade citation and an appendix entry with a provenance link to the passage location.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { citation: string, appendix_entry: { ref_id, publisher, date, methodology, link }, provenance_footnote: string }

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Drag recommendation into outline / open builder
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a board-prose drafting engine. Given selected recommendations, their evidence, and Dana's tone preferences, draft polished board-section narrative with embedded inline citation markers. Keep internal annotations structurally separable and excludable from sourced evidence.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Section: {section_title}. Recommendations: {recommendations_with_evidence}. Tone: measured, defensible, board-grade. Draft section prose with inline citation superscripts and flag any internal annotations as excludable notes.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { drafted_prose: string, citation_markers: [{ anchor_id, source_ref }], internal_notes: [{ note, excludable: true }] }

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a conflict-detection engine. Across cross-source signals scored for directional agreement, flag recommendations where sources materially disagree. Surface both sides rather than averaging into false consensus; produce a both-sides explanation.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Recommendations and their evidence directions: {recommendations_with_signal_directions}. Identify contested themes and produce a both-sides explanation for each.

ai_flows.fires_on_trigger: Set watch threshold on emerging theme
ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a continuous monitoring engine. Re-score sub-threshold emerging themes against newly ingested data and a user-defined confidence threshold. When a theme crosses its threshold, surface a threshold-crossing alert with the evidence that drove the momentum.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Watched theme: {theme}, threshold: {threshold}. Newly ingested signals: {new_signals}. Re-score current_confidence, momentum, and whether the threshold is crossed; cite driving evidence.
ai_flows.expected_response_shape: { theme, current_confidence: number, momentum: string, triggered: boolean, driving_evidence: [{ pull_quote, source_id }] }

brand_application.logo_treatment: NXT vector wordmark (BRAND_LOGO_SVG) rendered in the deep ink-blue masthead band at height 26px; CSS color set to paper (#FFFFFF) on the dark rail/masthead, ink (#141414) on light surfaces. Carrier-neutral — no third-party insurance brand. Wordmark sits left in the masthead with the '2026 Outlook' kicker in IBM Plex Mono, cyan (#00B7C3), 4px tracking, uppercase.
brand_application.voice_tone: Editorial, front-page-of-the-FT density — measured, board-grade, evidentiary calm. Every label earns its keep; the confidence badge is a thin ring, not a loud chip. Rigor over flash. The single amber pulse on provenance is the only attention-grabbing gesture.

quote.note: Paraphrased pull-quotes capped at 80 chars; cited evidence carries inline [n] marker

data.note: Tabular figures for confidence scores, relevance bars, sentiment values, recency tags; hero numeral capped at 36px in body weight, never out-ranks the 46px display title

_notes.ink_blue_masthead_override: #3A4A66 slate for the deep ink-blue header band per visual direction; wordmark in paper
_notes.cyan_evidence_panels: #00B7C3 reserved for evidence/source provenance chrome and citation anchors (<15% surface)
_notes.amber_provenance_pulse: #CC6644 rust — the single reserved expressive attention gesture on the cited passage
_notes.contested_badge: #CC6644 rust border + word 'Contested' + glyph, never color-alone
_notes.accent_usage: #B8B800 chartreuse on ONE primary CTA per screen + active confidence ring fill only; never as a text/border color on light (fails AA) — active links/states use cyan #00B7C3 or teal #115054
_notes.panel_wash: #F5F5F0 panel, #EBF7F8 wash-cool for evidence clusters, #FAF1EC wash-warn for contested dissent callouts
_notes.internal_annotation: #F2F1EA ecru fill + 3px slate #3A4A66 left rule — structurally separated from sourced evidence per hard constraint

critique.summary: The merged single-file prototype is coherent and runtime-correct. All 8 declared screens are present, registered in the App shell, and reachable via ScreenNav plus inter-screen dispatches (SELECT_REC, OPEN_PROVENANCE, SELECT_THEME, REFRESH, ADD_FLAG). Every dispatched action maps to a reducer case, and every state key read by screens exists in initialState. The root component is named App, hooks are used globally (useReducer/useState/useEffect/useMemo/useRef without React destructuring), framer-motion is accessed via window.framerMotion with a non-motion fallback, icons via window.lucide, and there are no import/export or render() statements. Seed data is deep: a named protagonist (Dana Reyes), 8 recommendations, 15 evidence items (all pull_quotes paraphrased and ≤80 chars), 6 sentiment series with 24 monthly values and labeled inflections, 7 sources with methodology + quality weights, flags, watch items with sparklines, contrib breakdown, diff rows, and export sections — concrete numbers throughout. Brand tokens (slate masthead, cyan evidence chrome, rust contested/provenance, single chartreuse CTA per screen, mono/Saira/Archivo fonts) are applied consistently; the Screen_theme_comparison_grid re-declares local TOK/FONT but with identical values, so no visual drift results. Session coverage is strong across modal/edge/tail buckets: contested both-sides callouts, confidence breakdown count-up, provenance amber pulse, stale-link guard, draft-preserved recovery note, account context indicator, keyboard/SR accessibility, AI multi-provider fallback, threshold alert banner that preserves work, and skeleton loaders. No blockers or integration drift requiring code changes were found.
